findings.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — Selecting Google Meet with an empty or missing destination array causes mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration to throw instead of falling back to Cal Video because optional chaining is missing.

Lark and BaseCalendarService have the same defect.

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73 — Event creation uses the first host’s destination calendar instead of the destination matching the active credential, causing secondary hosts to target another host’s calendar and potentially fail creation. Lark and BaseCalendarService have the same defect.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in Office365CalendarService.createEvent(), the code uses `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` which always takes the first destination calendar regardless of which credential is being used. Unlike GoogleCalendarService which was updated to accept a credentialId parameter and use `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` to match the correct calendar, Office365CalendarService, LarkCalendarService, and BaseCalendarService all just destructure the first element. This means for collective team events where multiple hosts have different destination calendars, secondary hosts would incorrectly target the first host's calendar instead of their own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:453 — Recurring-series cancellation processes only the organizer’s credentials and each booking’s first calendar reference, leaving additional collective hosts’ calendar events intact after their bookings are canceled.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in handleCancelBooking.ts around line 453, the code for recurring event cancellation (lines 430-456 in the new code) iterates through `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` which only contains the organizer's credentials. For each updated booking, it finds only the first calendar reference with `.find()` (line 441: `const bookingRef = updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes('_calendar'))`). This means for collective team events where multiple hosts have calendar events created (as supported by the new destinationCalendar array changes), only the organizer's calendar events would be deleted, leaving other team members' calendar events intact. The diff shows the system now supports multiple destination calendars for collective events (see handleNewBooking.ts changes with teamDestinationCalendars), but the cancellation logic wasn't updated to handle all calendar references.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1079 — When the organizer has no destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is null, so optional chaining silently discards collected teammates’ destinations instead of appending them to an initialized array.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff around line 1079 (in the actual diff context around lines 1060-1070), the code sets `destinationCalendar` to either `[eventType.destinationCalendar]`, `[organizerUser.destinationCalendar]`, or `null`. Then at line 1079 (shown in diff), there's `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. If neither eventType nor organizerUser has a destinationCalendar, `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, and the optional chaining `?.push()` will silently do nothing - the teamDestinationCalendars collected for COLLECTIVE scheduling will be discarded. The fix should initialize to an empty array `[]` instead of `null` when no organizer calendar exists, so team calendars can still be added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147 — Destinations without a credentialId cannot match the credential lookup, causing the legacy integration-based path to ignore the configured Google calendar and silently fall back to primary.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff at line 147 in GoogleCalendarService.ts, the code finds the calendar by matching credentialId: `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`. If no match is found, it falls back to 'primary'. The finding claims destinations without credentialId cause issues with 'legacy integration-based path', but the diff shows the createEvent method now receives credentialId as a parameter and uses it for lookup. The code correctly handles the case where no matching destination is found by using 'primary' as fallback. There is no 'legacy integration-based path' visible in this method that would be affected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:254 — When externalCalendarId is absent, the fallback searches for a destination matching that absent ID, preventing updates and deletes from targeting existing events on configured non-primary calendars.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 254 in the diff, the code is: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is absent/falsy, this fallback searches for a destination calendar where `externalId === undefined/null`, which will never match any real calendar entry. This means when no externalCalendarId is provided, the selectedCalendar will be undefined, causing updates to potentially fail or target the wrong calendar. The same bug pattern appears at line 314 for deleteEvent. This is a real logic error in the fallback mechanism.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — Non-calendar references receive credentialId: undefined, discarding result.credentialId for video integrations and preventing subsequent operations from identifying the account that created the meeting.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in packages/core/EventManager.ts around line 170, the code shows: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. This means for non-calendar types (video integrations), credentialId is explicitly set to undefined, discarding the result.credentialId value. The createEvent function in CalendarManager.ts now returns credentialId (line 267: `credentialId: credential.id`), but for video integrations this value is being thrown away. This could prevent subsequent operations from identifying which account created the meeting, which is a functional defect.
